505.body:
## Problem
In `apps/desktop` SSE `pump`, frame `data:` is `JSON.parse`d without try/catch. A single malformed frame ends the stream and drops the live run UI even when the server may still be running.

## Expected
A bad frame is skipped or counted, the pump continues (or one toast surfaces), and the run still reaches a terminal/handled state when the server finishes.

## Verification cases

1. **Malformed mid-stream frame**
   - **Preconditions:** Desktop workbench connected; a run is in flight with an open SSE stream.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Inject one malformed `data:` line mid-stream (invalid JSON).
     2. Observe UI and subsequent frames.
   - **Expected / pass:** Pump does not abort solely due to that frame; user sees at most one clear error/toast; later valid frames or a terminal settle still apply.

2. **Clean stream still works**
   - **Preconditions:** Same as (1), no injection.
   - **Steps:** Complete a normal turn end-to-end.
   - **Expected / pass:** Transcript, terminal status, and settle behave as today (no regression).

## Context
Follow-up from review of https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/499 (foundation). Out of that PR's Act-on scope; code-review inference on `api/stream.ts` pump.
505.title: [Bug] desktop: harden SSE frame JSON.parse so one bad frame does not end the run stream

506.body:
## Problem
Desktop workspace upload sends `File.name` into FormData without client-side basename sanitization. Path escape remains a server responsibility (`readWorkspaceFile` notes this), but a crafted name such as `../outside.txt` or a name containing `/` should be rejected or renamed on the client as defense in depth.

## Expected
Before upload, the client strips path segments / rejects unsafe names so only a basename reaches FormData; server still remains the authority and continues to rename/reject escapes.

## Verification cases

1. **Crafted relative name**
   - **Preconditions:** Open session with workspace panel; upload enabled (session not archived).
   - **Steps:**
     1. Upload (or simulate) a `File` whose `name` is `../outside.txt`.
     2. Inspect the FormData filename and the resulting workspace listing.
   - **Expected / pass:** Client does not send `../outside.txt` as-is (sanitize/reject); server listing shows no escape outside the session workspace.

2. **Name with slash**
   - **Preconditions:** Same as (1).
   - **Steps:** Upload a `File` whose `name` contains `/` (e.g. `a/b.txt`).
   - **Expected / pass:** Client basename-only or reject; no nested path created via the client name alone.

3. **Normal basename unchanged**
   - **Preconditions:** Same as (1).
   - **Steps:** Upload `notes.md`.
   - **Expected / pass:** File appears under the session workspace with the expected name (rename-on-conflict still applies).

## Context
Follow-up from review of https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/501. Non-blocking; server-side path authority noted in-PR.
506.title: [Bug] desktop: sanitize upload File.name basename before FormData (defense in depth)

507.author: HongyeZhou

## Problem
Settings › Runtime remote host credentials are write-only (good): empty fields keep the stored secret. The register/update API already accepts `password` / `passphrase` / `privateKeyPath: null` to forget, but the desktop UI never sends null, so there is no way to clear stored credentials from the dialog.

## Expected
A clear/forget control (or equivalent) sends null for the chosen secret fields so `hasPassword` / `hasPrivateKey` clear and later probes fail until a new secret is set.

## Verification cases

1. **Empty save keeps secret (current)**
   - **Preconditions:** Remote host with a stored password (`hasPassword` true).
   - **Steps:** Open credentials; leave password empty; save.
   - **Expected / pass:** `hasPassword` remains true (keep-on-empty behavior preserved).

2. **Explicit forget**
   - **Preconditions:** Same host with stored password.
   - **Steps:** Use the clear/forget control; save; re-open credentials / probe connect.
   - **Expected / pass:** `hasPassword` false; probe fails without a new secret.

3. **Re-set after forget**
   - **Preconditions:** Credentials cleared per (2).
   - **Steps:** Enter a new password; save; probe.
   - **Expected / pass:** `hasPassword` true; probe succeeds with the new secret.

## Context
Follow-up from review of https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/502. Out of Act-on scope for that PR (Escape stacking is in-scope there).

## Problem

Daily real-research shards fail during dependency preparation on the current `ubuntu-latest` image (Ubuntu 26.04, CPython 3.14.4), before any model calls. `.ci/prepare-real-research.sh` creates a venv using the runner interpreter and installs `numpy==2.2.6` and `scipy==1.15.3`. The same main commit (`7ee6c1d0bcc8374062364d51b3f4dfdf87a1396d`) passed dependency preparation on Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.12.3 on October 20 and failed on Ubuntu 26.04 / Python 3.14.4 on October 21. Evidence: [October 21 run](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/39666641312), [October 23 run](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40014929958).

Support the new Ubuntu image and Python 3.14 rather than downgrading the runner or interpreter. Update the benchmark dependency preparation to a compatible, reproducible dependency set and check its direct consumers.

## Acceptance criteria

- The benchmark numerical dependencies install successfully on Ubuntu 26.04 / Python 3.14 without an accidental source-build requirement for the obsolete pins.
- DRB and Biomni benchmark preparation and evaluator imports remain compatible with the selected dependencies.
- Add focused validation that catches this compatibility failure without making model calls.
- Keep the real-case assertions and evidence requirements intact. Model gateway billing failures and previously fixed runner cleanup behavior are outside this change.

519.author: zhaozhaozz
519.body:
## 范围与证据

汇总 [2026-10-24 Nightly run 40121906605](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605) 的三项剩余问题。运行版本：`9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be`。

#514 / #515 修复的 Ubuntu 26.04 / Python 3.14 依赖准备已通过，本次不再作为阻塞项。以下区分实际运行结果与源码诊断，不据此认定所有 main CI 都失败。

- 此前的计划、follow-up、reload 断言已通过；失败后的切回原会话及位置保持断言尚未执行，不能算通过。
- #511 仍讨论编号集合与排序的 UX 口径，本 issue 不替它决定方案，只修复测试对已实现显示规则的错误假设。

## 2. 已执行失败的分片被汇总成 NOT_RUN

[research-8 结果 artifact 12574909042](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/artifacts/12574909042) 的 `e2e-real/tagged/summary.json` 明确记录：

但 [汇总 job 120992446082](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/job/120992446082) 输出 executed=18/19、passed=18，并将该用例标为 `NOT_RUN`。

源码诊断：[`.ci/real-report.mjs:19-24`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9eb45d753b86b94ce67d41032d9511d724c628be/.ci/real-report.mjs#L19-L24) 在失败分片的 `results.push(...summary.results)` 之前抛出 `SHARD_FAILED`，丢掉了其已执行结果。需要保留身份、版本、digest 等校验通过的失败证据，同时继续让 gate 失败。该运行应准确呈现 19 executed、18 passed、1 failed，而不是将执行失败混同为未运行。

## 3. 两项 UT 等待完成超时，原因待查

[UT job 120955273894](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/job/120955273894)：4754 planned / 4754 executed / 4752 passed / 2 failed / 0 skipped。

[UT artifact 12572160563](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40121906605/artifacts/12572160563) 中的实际失败：

- `ut/tagged/group-279/worker-1-events.jsonl`：`services/api/src/evolution/orchestrator.test.ts` 的 `a measured run is staged before the sidecar is asked to start`，报 `timed out waiting for the run to settle`。
- `ut/tagged/group-343/worker-1-events.jsonl`：`services/api/src/server.test.ts` 的 `running sessions accept queued runs and start them after the active run completes`，报等待 run 进入 `completed` 超时。

[同一 SHA 较早的 UT job 120785725594](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40064771478/job/120785725594) 在 Ubuntu 26.04 上 4754/4754 通过。现有证据不能区分测试时序、环境或产品状态推进问题，不认定为负载抖动或确定性回归。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 会话切换测试按当前显示规则及明确的 Session 身份校验，补齐“新增会话 → 切回原会话 → 原计划/时间线位置保持”的验证；不删除原行为断言。

538.author: HongyeZhou
538.body:
## Problem

PR #534 copies a redacted diagnostic to the clipboard and pre-fills a **public** GitHub new-issue URL. Token/secret/Bearer/URL-userinfo redaction is covered, but absolute filesystem paths that embed a username (for example `/home/<user>/...`, `/Users/<user>/...`, `C:\Users\<user>\...`) can still appear in the error title/detail and therefore in the clipboard and the draft URL. That leaks local identity/PII to a public tracker without the user noticing.

This is adjacent to #58 / #534 but was not part of the listed Security acceptance bullets (Authorization/Bearer, token, secret, password, cookie, URL userinfo).

## Expected

Before truncation and before building the GitHub issue URL, diagnostic text (and any exported log metadata strings) must redact home-directory / username path segments so a public draft cannot carry the local account name. Other redaction already required by #58 stays in place.

## Verification cases

1. **Unix home path in error detail**
   - Preconditions: Web UI shows a visible error whose detail contains `/home/alice/.sciencediscovery-data/logs/api.log` (or equivalent fixture).
   - Steps: Click **Copy key diagnostics**; open the GitHub issue draft from the same control.
   - Expected / pass: Clipboard and issue-draft body contain a redacted path form (for example `/home/[REDACTED]/...` or equivalent); the literal username `alice` does not appear. Bundle stays within the existing 4000 / 6500 caps.

2. **macOS / Windows user path**
   - Preconditions: Error detail contains `/Users/bob/project/file.ts` and `C:\Users\bob\AppData\...`.
   - Steps: Copy diagnostics and open the issue draft.
   - Expected / pass: `bob` does not appear in clipboard or draft URL/body; redaction markers are present.

3. **Negative — non-home path retained**
   - Preconditions: Error detail contains a non-user path such as `/tmp/sciencediscovery-test/out.log` or `/var/log/...` with no username segment.
   - Steps: Copy diagnostics.
   - Expected / pass: Path remains useful for maintainers (not over-redacted into uselessness); still no tokens/secrets.

4. **Regression — existing secret redaction**
   - Preconditions: Detail includes `Bearer sk-testsecret` and `api_key=private-value`.
   - Steps: Copy + open issue draft.
   - Expected / pass: Secrets remain `[REDACTED]`; path redaction does not disable prior rules.

## Context

Refs #534 (feat: copy sanitized error diagnostics). Related #58. Security hardening for the public GitHub draft destination.
538.title: [Bug] Redact home-directory and username path segments in error diagnostic bundles

541.author: zhaozhaozz
541.body:
## Problem

After a remote Shell Execution is accepted, a lost status observation is recorded in two places that disagree.

The shell execution record becomes `unknown` / `unconfirmed`. That means the remote result has not been confirmed. It does not mean the command failed. Inspecting that execution reconciles the record with the Runner by the same Execution ID and does not resubmit the command (see #185).

The provenance execution run written when that observation throws is different. The dispatch error path appends an execution run with `status: "failed"`, `exitCode: null`, and stderr set to the observation error. `ExecutionRun.status` only allows `succeeded`, `failed`, and `cancelled`. Runs are append-only, so a later reconciliation that adopts the Runner's committed result updates the shell execution record and leaves this run unchanged.

Skill distillation and the memory graph read execution runs. They can treat an unconfirmed observation as a job failure, and they still see that failure after the shell execution record has been reconciled to the Runner's real outcome.

## Expected

- An observation that stays unconfirmed is not reported as a successful job or as a failed job by the execution-run record, by skill distillation, or by the memory graph.
- If reconciliation later adopts a committed Runner result for that same Execution ID, those readers see that result.
- A Runner outcome that really failed or was cancelled, including a non-zero exit or a recorded failure with a committed version, is still stored as failed or cancelled.
- The command is not replayed.

## Note

#185 does not choose how to represent an unconfirmed run. `ExecutionRun.status` has no value for "not confirmed", and the run list is append-only. This issue tracks that choice. It is separate from the shell-execution reconciliation fix.
541.title: [Bug] An unconfirmed shell observation is stored as a failed execution run

`skills/report-writer/SKILL.md` contains 11 fenced-code markers (` ``` `):

| Line | Pair |

559.author: JinhZhao
559.body:
`docs/en/advanced-setup/configure-skills.md:7` tells users to provide a non-empty `description` in the skill frontmatter.

However, `packages/specialist/src/skills.ts:565` defaults `description` to `""`:

```typescript
const description = typeof parsed.frontmatter.description === "string"
  ? parsed.frontmatter.description
  : "";
```

And `validateSkillPackage` (`:529-628`) performs no emptiness or minimum-length check on the value. A skill with an empty description passes validation and packages cleanly.

Since `description` is what the selector prompt uses to decide whether a skill is relevant to a user request, an empty description silently drops the skill out of routing — the skill exists but is never selected.

**Reproduce:** Create a minimal SKILL.md with no `description` field; run `validateSkillPackage`.

**Suggested fix:** Either reject empty descriptions in `validateSkillPackage` (matching the doc), or correct the doc to state that description is optional.
559.title: [Bug] validateSkillPackage accepts empty description that docs forbid

560.author: JinhZhao
560.body:
`skills/citation-reviewer/SKILL.md:17-20` instructs the reviewer to classify identity and availability failures as `CITATION_IDENTIFIER_MISMATCH`, `CITATION_IDENTIFIER_NOT_RESOLVED`, and `CITATION_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`.

The runtime whitelist contains only `CITATION_CLAIM_NOT_SUPPORTED` (`packages/provenance/src/citation-review.ts:39-41`), and other codes are dropped at `:133-136`, setting an internal `discardedUnverifiedFinding` flag.

We read the comment at `:35-38` and agree with the design intent: identity resolution is established by the execution layer before the model sees a source snapshot, and a provider failure is not evidence of a bad citation. This is not a request to change that policy.

However, the current design treats unverifiable content as if it never existed. When a citation identity cannot be resolved, or a provider fails, the reader sees no signal that the system tried and could not confirm. In a citation-dense report — for example, two near-duplicate ACS papers on the same catalytic system whose DOIs are confused — the suppressed case is precisely the one worth showing, because it tells the reader that identity resolution failed for this cluster and coverage is accordingly limited.

**Suggested fix:** Add `UNVERIFIABLE` (or `IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED` / `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`) to `EvidenceAssessment` (`packages/schema/src/provenance.ts:177`), so that suppressed findings are recorded as evidence with a visible status rather than silently dropped. The review summary could then report "N identity/availability findings suppressed as UNVERIFIABLE" with reasons, and the Skill text would align with the runtime instead of asking the model for codes it can never act on.

**Related:** #414 (review depth), but this is a schema-level gap, not a review-quality issue.
560.title: [Feature] Evidence grading should express UNVERIFIABLE status, not silently drop uncertain findings

561.author: JinhZhao
561.body:
`packages/model/src/client.ts:171-174` already documents the problem:

> "A reasoning model bills its hidden thought against this same budget, so the default that is comfortable for a chat reply can be exhausted before the first visible character."

`packages/model/src/usage.ts:32-100` normalizes usage into `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `totalTokens` (plus cache fields), but does not extract `reasoning_tokens` from the API response — even though the raw response includes it (e.g., `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` for OpenAI-compatible, `output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` for Responses API). The test file (`usage.test.ts:15,17`) confirms the raw data is present but discarded during normalization.

For thinking-model workloads (GLM-Pro, DeepSeek R1, QwQ), this means:

1. The shared `maxTokens` budget (default 16,384) can be exhausted by reasoning alone, producing empty outputs
2. There is no visibility into how much of the budget reasoning consumed
3. Users cannot tune reasoning vs. output budgets independently

**Suggested fix:**

1. Extract `reasoning_tokens` from the API response into `NormalizedUsage` (e.g., a `reasoningTokens` field)
2. Consider separate budget configuration for reasoning and output tokens, or raise the default `maxTokens` for known reasoning models
3. Surface reasoning token consumption in run diagnostics so users can identify budget exhaustion

**Context:** Discovered during a 4-round evaluation of ScienceDiscovery for catalysis research workflows (44 runs, 2 models). Thinking-model runs (GLM-Pro) spent up to 60 minutes in planning loops where reasoning tokens consumed the entire budget before any visible output was produced.
561.title: [Feature] Token budget should separate reasoning and output tokens for thinking models

563.author: zhaozhaozz
563.body:
## Summary

On 2026-10-26 every GitHub issue in `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` was classified against the nine requirement rows in #249. Pull requests were excluded. The three counts agreed: `gh issue list --state all`, REST pagination of 100 items per page, and the issue search counter. The total is **232** issues, **116 open** and **116 closed**.

Whether an issue is developed was judged from `origin/main` at `65eddde1`, not from the open or closed flag. An open issue can already be on `main`. A closed issue can still be undeveloped when it was closed as a duplicate or as not planned, or when the change never reached `main`.

This issue records that snapshot. It does not close, retitle, or implement any of the issues below.

## Counts

| | |
| --- | --- |
| bug / feature / other | 73 / 151 / 8 |
| bug severity P0 / P1 / P2 / P3 | 1 / 24 / 44 / 4 |
| mapped to a #249 row / unmapped | 139 / 93 |
| developed / partial / not developed / not applicable | 103 / 39 / 82 / 8 |
| marked complex | 122 |

Severity is the impact of the defect itself. It is not lowered because a later commit fixed it. "Not applicable" is used only for the eight items in **other**, which have no defect or feature to build. ## What I was trying to do

## Original specification (preserved for traceability)

## Summary

`/evolve` is one of the largest features in the product and has **no user documentation in either language**. A researcher cannot learn what it does, when to reach for it, or how to drive it, without reading the source. I would like an explanation page, a how-to, and a tutorial — in English and Chinese — plus the existing Chinese architecture note fixed up and made reachable.

## What ships versus what is documented

What ships:

| Surface | Size |
|---|---|
| `services/evolve` Python sidecar | 23 modules, two search engines — flat-PUCT (`puct_engine.py`) and MAP-Elites islands with ring migration (`openevolve_engine.py`) |
| Scoring modes | four domain seams: `scorecard_domain` (dataset metric), `test_gate_domain` (test suite), `script_domain` (a scorer the model writes), `judge_domain` (LLM rubric) |
| Agent tools | `create_evolve_run`, `get_evolve_run` |
| Skill | `evolve-design`, a four-checkpoint design conversation with an algorithm choice |
| Web UI | 13 components — panel, algorithm picker, candidate stream, score chart, search graph canvas and table, budget bar, cell grid |
| UI strings | 188 `evolve.*` message keys |
| HTTP API | `/api/evolve/runs`, `/runs/<id>/events`, `/runs/<id>/candidates/<hash>`, `/runs/<id>/stop` |

What is documented:

| Language | Coverage |
|---|---|
| Chinese | **one** file, `docs/zh/explanation/evolve-standalone.md` (252 lines) |
| English | **zero** — the word "evolve" appears in exactly one English file, `docs/en/reference/web-frontend.md`, in passing |

And the single Chinese file has two problems of its own:

1. **It is unreachable.** `docs/zh/explanation/README.md` does not link it. The index lists `skill-library-management.md` and `skill-self-evolution.md` but not `evolve-standalone.md`, so the only way to find it is to list the directory. (Raised as an orphan page in [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25).)
2. **It answers a different question.** Its own opening says it covers the two engines' differences and what it would take to run the sidecar as a standalone backend. That is an architecture note for a maintainer. Nothing in it tells a researcher what a search is for, when scoring will actually discriminate, or how to start one.

## What to write

### 1. `explanation/evolve.md` (EN + ZH)

What an evolution search is, and the honest limits: it rewrites a candidate dozens of times and keeps what scores higher, so it succeeds or fails on whether the scoring can tell a good candidate from a bad one — a scoring function that cannot shows up as a flat run, not as an error. Cover the four scoring modes and when each applies, the two engines and when to pick which, and the frozen-scorer rule that `test_gate_domain` enforces, whose upstream note is worth quoting: *"without it the shortest path to a high score is to weaken the thing measuring it."*

### 2. `how-to/run-an-evolution-search.md` (EN + ZH)

The operational path: preparing a starting point and a dataset or test suite, what `--algorithm puct` versus `--algorithm openevolve` changes, reading the score chart and the search graph, budgets and stopping, retrieving the winning candidate, and what the approval card asks for before a run starts.

### 3. `tutorial/…-evolve-a-solution.md` (EN + ZH)

One short end-to-end run a reader can actually complete: a small starting program, a dataset with a metric, the `/evolve-design` conversation answered checkpoint by checkpoint, then what to look at while it runs and how to tell a real improvement from noise. This is the piece [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) asks for in general, applied here.

### 4. Fix what exists

Link `evolve-standalone.md` from the Chinese explanation index, give it an English counterpart, and retitle it so its scope is obvious — it is the engine-internals and standalone-deployment note, not the feature's documentation.

### 5. Reference the surface

The four HTTP endpoints belong in `reference/rest-api.md`, and the two agent tools in `reference/builtin-tools.md`, so the feature is reachable from the reference tree as well as the prose.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An English reader can learn what `/evolve` is, when to use it, and how to run one, without reading source code.
- [ ] Explanation, how-to and tutorial pages exist in both languages and are linked from their indexes.
- [ ] The four scoring modes and the two engines are each documented with the case they suit.
- [ ] The frozen-scorer rule is stated where a user designing a search will meet it.
- [ ] The tutorial runs end to end on a supplied example, and says how to judge whether the result is real.
- [ ] `evolve-standalone.md` is linked, translated, and scoped by its title.
- [ ] The evolve endpoints and agent tools appear in the reference documents.

## Open questions

- Should the tutorial evolve a program (dataset metric) or a prompt (LLM judge)? The program case is more convincing; the prompt case is cheaper to run and needs no dataset.
- Can a small example — a starting program plus a labelled dataset — be committed for the tutorial, as [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) proposes generally?
- Does the Idea Tree engine want the same treatment in the same pass? It has the same shape of gap: `idea-tree-engine.md` is also Chinese-only.

Related: [#25](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/25) (documentation completeness and the orphan pages), [#26](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/26) (the tutorial series), [#54](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/54) (RSI, which builds directly on this engine and will be much harder to explain if the engine itself is undocumented).

## Cross-check needed

cc @zhaozhaozz @zy95-12 @HongyeZhou

### Three-layer defaults (important)
These coexist and are easy to conflate:

1. **Schema fallback**: `DEFAULT_SKILL_SELECTION_MODE = "all"` when unset (`packages/schema/src/runtime-settings.ts`).
2. **New Project product default**: `withDefaultProjectSkillSettings` writes `skillSelectionMode: "selected"` + empty `enabledSkillIds` / libraries (Skill Library intent: avoid silently expanding capability).
3. **JiuwenSwarm force-all**: on start, `http/index.ts` calls `store.useEverySkillEverywhere()` so the **effective** mode is `all` while Swarm is the backend (stored `selected` is kept and applies again when switching back to native).

Box smoke on Swarm therefore seeing `all` is **expected**, not accidental.

### Observation (box smoke, 2026-10-24 Asia/Shanghai)
- SHA: `main@9eb45d75`
- Backend: **JiuwenSwarm** (force-all path)
- Model: Zhipu `glm-5.3-flash`
- ~17 shipped skills effective, `thinkingEffort: high`
- Trivial user prompt → **~38k input tokens** (chat/history ≈ **165 bytes**)
- First visible assistant text ≈ **20s** wall

Progressive disclosure is **already implemented** (`docs/en/developer-docs/skill-progressive-disclosure.md`: metadata/path in prompt, body on demand). It does **not** prevent metadata/tool-surface growth when the effective selected set is the whole catalog under `all` / Swarm force-all.

### Questions for maintainers
1. Should end-user UX optimize for **Project `selected`** or accept **Swarm force-all** as the primary path?
2. Is there appetite to change schema DEFAULT, Swarm force-all, or both?
3. Have you seen the same **TTFT / cost** under Swarm vs native?

### Proposed performance watch split (do not mix into one Nightly bucket)
1. **UX / API latency lane** — queue → context → **TTFT** → run wall; short daily probe (`live.mjs ttft` + one real short chat), measure under **both** native and JiuwenSwarm, and under `all` vs `selected`.
2. **Correctness lane (existing L3 ×9)** — tool/files/cancel/etc.; keep **out of** TTFT gates.
3. **Research quality lane (L4 Nightly)** — DRB/Biomni/etc. as quality signal, **not** first-token UX.

### Possible directions (not proposing a fix yet)
- Keep progressive disclosure; also shrink **effective set** under Swarm (or stop force-all)
- Align schema DEFAULT with new-Project `selected`
- Cap / warn when resolved skill metadata size exceeds a threshold
- Surface skill-token cost in Usage / composer

### Non-goals
- Nightly research-bench red streak root-cause (separate)
- Tool-call accuracy eval (separate)

### Test coverage gap
- Unit coverage exists for settings semantics (`store.test.ts`: selected / all / `useEverySkillEverywhere`).
- **No CI gate** on TTFT or skill-token size; `live.mjs ttft()` logs only.
- Progressive disclosure tests do not cap catalog size under `all`.

Cross-check so far: skills-side review agrees the three-layer story; DigitalMate has no parallel issue. Nearby: #508, #93, #141.

## Problem
A Windows durability fix for CAS directory `fsync` (`O_RDWR` on `win32` because `FlushFileBuffers` needs a writable handle) and `toNamespacedPath` for SQLite paths landed inside the conversational-configuration protocol PR (#553), mixed with unrelated schema/protocol work. On Linux the `win32` branch is never taken, so CI here cannot exercise the failure mode (silently weaker directory sync if the open/handle is wrong).

## Expected
- CAS Windows durable-directory sync ships in its own small PR (or clearly scoped commit series) with Windows verification attached.
- Configuration/protocol PRs do not carry unrelated CAS durability changes.

## Verification cases
1. **Writable-directory sync on Windows**
   - Preconditions: Windows host; CAS `VersionStore` / `RefStore` initialized on a normal NTFS directory.
   - Steps: Create/update a live ref that triggers `syncDirectory`; confirm no throw from `open(..., O_RDWR|O_DIRECTORY)` + `handle.sync()`.
   - Expected / pass: Operation succeeds; refs.sqlite and object dirs remain consistent after process kill mid-write (WAL + FULL sync still hold).
2. **Long / namespaced path**
   - Preconditions: Windows; store path that needs `\\?\` / namespaced form (deep or near-MAX_PATH tree).
   - Steps: Open `RefStore` / lease DBs via the same helpers.
   - Expected / pass: `DatabaseSync(toNamespacedPath(...))` opens; no path-not-found solely from missing namespace prefix.
3. **Negative — read-only directory**
   - Preconditions: Directory without write ACL for the process.
   - Steps: Trigger `syncDirectory`.
   - Expected / pass: Failure is loud (thrown/propagated), not a silent no-op sync; caller sees the error.
4. **Linux unchanged**
   - Preconditions: Linux CI/dev.
   - Steps: Same CAS unit/integration paths as today.
   - Expected / pass: Still uses `O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY`; no behavioral change.

## Context
Refs #553 (CAS hunks in `packages/cas/src/versioning.ts`, `workspace-lease.ts`, `workspace-lifecycle.ts`). Spotted during review of the four-PR configuration stack; out of scope for the shared configuration protocol.

When there is clear association evidence that a later call is a bounded correction of the same logical tool operation, the UI updates in place (or equivalent merged presentation): default view is a concise result; attempt count / errors / recovery detail are available on demand. Unrecoverable failures keep a clear reason. Real execution history and audit evidence are not rewritten as pure success. Do not blindly replay side-effecting operations to reduce cards.

## Verification cases

1. **In-place recovery presentation**
   - **Preconditions:** A recoverable invalid-argument or soft-fail path that retries within one logical operation (browser or hermetic UI fixture).
   - **Steps:**
     1. Trigger a tool call that fails then succeeds on a bounded correction.
     2. Inspect the timeline/card for that operation.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Default view is not a stack of contradictory failed+success cards for the same operation; recovery state/result is shown in place; history of attempts remains inspectable; independent operations are not wrongly merged.

2. **Side-effect boundary**
   - **Preconditions:** A tool invocation that may have already executed with side effects before observation failed.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Observe recovery/UI merge behavior.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** No blind resubmit of committed side-effecting work solely to tidy the timeline; audit/failure records stay consistent.

## Context
- Env: _not provided_ for a fresh UI journey this filing; scope from #335 expected narrative and product phase-3 note on that Issue.
- Refs: Parent #335; PRs #345 / #551 (merged) for prompt-path only.
- Notes: Related UX umbrella #330 is adjacent (timeline hierarchy) but not a substitute for this recovery-presentation bug.
591.title: [Feature] clearer fail-then-retry timeline narrative for tool recovery (from #335 S6)

## Problem
PR #460 isolates the embedded JiuwenSwarm default local runtime under `$HOME/.sciencediscovery/jiuwenswarm` and documents Docker’s persisted HOME layout. Local coexistence was verified; the **Docker persisted-volume restart** journey was **BLOCKED** (no container engine/socket on the author host) and remains an explicit leftover acceptance item on #257 / #460.

## Expected
After a container restart that keeps the documented persisted volume, ScienceDiscovery’s embedded Swarm registry, workspaces, and related runtime state remain under the SD-owned layout, still isolated from any standalone Swarm data, and SD continues to use its own instance endpoints without adopting a sibling standalone instance.

## Verification cases

1. **Docker volume restart persistence**
   - **Preconditions:** Container-capable host; ScienceDiscovery Docker path with persisted volume as documented after #460; disposable standalone Swarm data available to prove non-interference if co-tested.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Start SD via the Docker path; record embedded registry/workspace identity and a distinguishing config marker.
     2. Restart the container with the same persisted volume.
     3. Confirm SD still binds to the same embedded instance data and does not read/write standalone Swarm registry/config.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Persisted SD state survives restart; isolation from standalone Swarm holds; no silent reconnect to another Swarm service.

## Context
- Env: Author host for #460 lacked container engine/socket; residual Docker journey _not provided_ here beyond that BLOCKED note.
- Refs: Parent #257; fixing PR #460 (merged). Local default-namespace isolation landed in #460; this Issue tracks Docker restart verification only.
592.title: [Bug] Verify Docker persisted-volume restart for embedded JiuwenSwarm after #460

593.author: HongyeZhou
593.body:
## Problem
PR #460 delivered default local namespace isolation for embedded JiuwenSwarm. The product decision on #257 requires a **complete config/runtime boundary**, not only a renamed default directory: SD must not silently adopt standalone Swarm configuration via inherited env vars, home/registry lookup, or runtime service discovery, and must not let port collision silently attach SD to another Swarm service.

## Expected
- Embedded Swarm config and state are owned by ScienceDiscovery; discovering a user’s standalone Swarm (including same instance name) must not replace or merge SD’s model/skill/agent/tool behavior.
- Outer-process Swarm-specific environment variables, default SDK paths, and service discovery must not bypass the SD-owned boundary unless the user explicitly configured an SD-supported override with clear ownership.
- setup/start/status/env/stop, logs, and connection endpoints resolve to the same SD-owned instance; port conflicts are handled without silently connecting to a sibling Swarm.

## Verification cases

1. **Standalone config does not drive SD**
   - **Preconditions:** Disposable home/namespace; standalone Swarm instance (including same name `sciencediscovery`) with deliberately different identifiable config.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Start ScienceDiscovery with default embedded settings.
     2. Change standalone model/skill/agent settings and start/stop the standalone instance.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** SD behavior and backend ownership remain SD’s; standalone changes do not alter SD settings or which instance SD uses.

2. **Env / discovery bypass**
   - **Preconditions:** Outer environment carries standalone Swarm-specific variables and/or occupied ports that could point at a non-SD instance.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Launch SD without an explicit user opt-in to that standalone endpoint.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** SD does not silently read standalone registry/config or connect to the foreign service; conflicts surface safely rather than mis-binding.

3. **SD lifecycle leaves standalone intact**
   - **Preconditions:** Both SD embedded and standalone instances live in the disposable namespace.
   - **Steps:**
     1. Run SD setup/start/stop and change SD settings.
   - **Expected result / pass criteria:** Standalone registry/config/sessions remain unmodified and the standalone process is not stopped by SD lifecycle.

## Context
- Env: Evidence from #257 product decision comment (`embedded-swarm-isolation-decision`) and #460 partial scope (local isolation done; broader boundary still called out).
- Refs: Parent #257; fixing PR #460 (merged). Default path isolation landed in #460; this Issue tracks remaining boundary / env / discovery acceptance from that decision.
- Notes: Do not auto-migrate or delete ambiguous standalone data. Explicit SD-supported overrides remain allowed when ownership is clear.
593.title: [Bug] Embedded JiuwenSwarm must not adopt standalone config via env or discovery

595.author: HongyeZhou
595.body:
## Problem

PR #552 delivers standalone (inbox / 最近会话) chats and project folds, but membership is fixed at create time. Users still cannot move an existing recent conversation into a new or existing project without losing history or artifacts. That remaining acceptance item from #305 is out of scope for #552.

## Expected

A reader can move a standalone (recent / inbox) conversation into a new or existing project, and optionally move between projects or back to Recent, without losing messages, artifacts, or workspace accounting. Navigation and session lists stay consistent (no duplicate rows).

## Verification cases

1. **Move into existing project**
   - **Preconditions:** One Recent/inbox session with messages and at least one artifact; project P already exists.
   - **Steps:** From that session, choose move into project P (or equivalent UI).
   - **Expected / pass:** Session appears under P; history and artifacts intact; no longer listed under 最近会话; session bar / active project shows P.

2. **Move into newly created project**
   - **Preconditions:** One standalone session with history.
   - **Steps:** Move → create project with name only → confirm.
   - **Expected / pass:** Project created; session inside it; history/artifacts intact; gone from Recent.

3. **Move between projects / back to Recent**
   - **Preconditions:** Session already under a project.
   - **Steps:** Move to another project, then back to Recent (if supported).
   - **Expected / pass:** Membership updates; no duplicate rows in sidebar; workspace path and accounting remain consistent.

4. **E2E first-run remainder of #305**
   - **Preconditions:** Fresh user with no projects.
   - **Steps:** Start chat without a project → later move that chat into a project.
   - **Expected / pass:** Covers the #305 E2E acceptance remainder that #552 intentionally deferred.

## Context

- Refs #305 (remaining AC: organize / move conversations into projects later).
- Follow-up from review of https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/552 (`bde9143`); not blocking that PR.
595.title: [Feature] Move a standalone (recent) conversation into a project
